a: The Hope Highway, also referred to as the Hope Road Turnoff, is a Forest Highway situated in the Kenai Peninsula Borough in the U.S. state of Alaska. It links the city of Hope with the Seward Highway, running for 17 miles (27 km) through the Chugach National Forest. Along its route, the road passes the ghost town of Sunrise City as well as several smaller settlements, all of which are remnants of the gold rush that took place in the area. The highway was built around 1928 and was designated Forest Highway 14 by the Federal Highway Administration.
h: The Hope Highway , also known as the Hope Road Turnoff , is a Forest Highway located in the Kenai Peninsula Borough , in the U.S. state of Alaska . The road passes the ghost town of Sunrise City and several smaller settlements , remnants of the gold rush that occurred in that area . The highway was created circa 1928 and was designated as Forest Highway 14 by the Federal Highway Administration .

a: The uprising against Porfirio Díaz's government began in late 1910, after Díaz had imprisoned his rival Francisco Madero and declared himself the winner of a fraudulent election. Madero had previously drawn many followers with vague pledges of agrarian reform. He managed to escape from prison and fled to Texas, where he issued his celebrated Plan of San Luis Potosí. This manifesto urged an armed revolt against the Porfiriato and the establishment of free, democratic elections. In response to Madero's proclamation, violent clashes erupted across Mexico in November 1910.
h: The rebellion against the government of Porfirio Díaz broke out in late 1910 , after Díaz had his rival Francisco Madero imprisoned and had announced his own victory in a falsified election . Madero 's earlier vague promises of agrarian reforms had attracted many supporters . He himself escaped from prison and fled to Texas , from where he issued his famous Plan of San Luis Potosí . This manifesto called for an armed uprising against the Porfiriato and establishment of free and democratic elections . As a response to Madero 's proclamation , violent clashes began throughout Mexico in November 1910 .

h: A more recent theory , with broad support among archaeologists , is that Celtic culture and language arrived in Ireland as a result of cultural diffusion . a: While wintering in Africa, the corn crake inhabits dry grassland and savanna, favoring vegetation 30 to 200 cm (0.98 to 6.56 ft) tall, including areas that have been seasonally burnt and, on occasion, sedges or reed beds. It also turns up in fallow and abandoned fields, uncut grass on airfields, and the margins of crops. In South Africa it has been recorded at altitudes of at least 1,750 metres (5,740 ft). Each individual confines itself to a relatively small area. Although it is sometimes found alongside the African crake, that species generally favors moister, shorter grassland than the corn crake does. During migration, the corn crake may additionally be encountered in wheatfields and around golf courses.
